name: How to Avoid Common Mistakes in Finish Carpentry Coordination

step.name: Step 1
step.text: Finish carpentry is where your vision really comes to life, but a few missteps can throw the whole project off track. One common mistake we see is starting finish work before the substrate prep is actually complete. This is a big one because if your walls aren't properly prepped, your trim and cabinets won't sit right, leading to frustrating delays and a less-than-perfect finish. Another frequent issue is failing to coordinate with other trades still active on the job. You don't want your painter bumping into the finish carpenter or vice-versa, as it can cause damage or slow everyone down. Skipping a detailed closeout inspection is also a pitfall; you need to walk through the job with your contractor to check alignment, gaps, hardware, and surface quality. Lastly, not documenting the scope, timeline, and how changes will be handled in writing is a recipe for misunderstandings. A clear, detailed contract protects everyone and keeps the project moving smoothly. We're very involved daily to ensure quality and prevent these kinds of headaches. To keep your project on track, make sure all these coordination points are handled meticulously. If you're tackling a complex remodel, consider bringing in a pro like us; we serve the entire East Bay Area and can handle these intricate details for you.
